purpose: Independent practice of A10.2 — comparing length. Used as Lesson 1 consolidation artifact and as evidence for the diagnostic checklist.
student_learning_goal: I can compare how long things are.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can compare how long things are.
header.character_watermark: Max the Measure Moose in the top-right corner of the header, holding a measuring stick. Small (~1.5in tall). References blueprint.recurring_characters.

parts.student_instructions: Look at each pair. Circle the LONGER object.
parts.visual_layout: Five paired-object rows stacked vertically. Each row shows two objects side by side, lined up at the left edge: (1) pencil vs marker, (2) ribbon vs string, (3) snake vs worm, (4) hockey stick vs paint brush, (5) two same-length blocks. Each pair ~3in × 1in.

image_placeholders.description: Five paired-object rows in B&W line art for a Kindergarten worksheet, each row ~3in × 1in. Each pair shows two objects lined up at the left edge so the student can compare lengths visually. Row 1: short pencil + long marker. Row 2: short ribbon + long ribbon. Row 3: short worm + long snake. Row 4: short paint brush + long hockey stick. Row 5: two equal-length blocks. Generous spacing between rows for the child to circle.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P1_PAIRS at Part 1: instructions ask the child to circle the longer object. Keywords name the pairs shown — children compare specific object pairs (pencil vs marker, ribbon pairs).

parts.answer_key: Row 1: marker. Row 2: long ribbon. Row 3: snake. Row 4: hockey stick. Row 5: SAME — neither is longer. Accept circling either or both for Row 5.

parts.visual_layout: Four horizontal strips of varied lengths stacked vertically. Each strip is a thin solid B&W rectangle, all aligned at the left edge. Lengths: 1in, 2in, 3in, 5in (in mixed order). Beside each strip is a small numbered box for the child to write 1, 2, 3, or 4.

image_placeholders.description: Four horizontal strips in B&W line art for a Kindergarten worksheet, stacked vertically and aligned at the left edge. Lengths in display order (top to bottom): 3in, 1in, 5in, 2in (mixed so children must reason). Each strip ~0.4in tall, thin solid border. Beside each strip, a small empty box (~0.5in × 0.5in) for the child to write a number from 1 (shortest) to 4 (longest).
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P2_STRIPS at Part 2: instructions ask the child to order strips by length. Keywords name the visual elements (strips) and the comparison endpoints (shortest, longest).

parts.student_instructions: Look around your classroom. Find 2 things that are the SAME length. Draw them.
parts.visual_layout: Two blank drawing boxes side by side, each ~3in × 2in with thin solid border. Below each box is a label line for the child to write the object's name.

image_placeholders.description: Two blank drawing boxes side by side for a Kindergarten worksheet. Each box is ~3in × 2in with a thin solid border. Below each box, a horizontal line for writing the object's name. Designed for the child to draw two same-length classroom items.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P3_BOXES at Part 3: instructions ask the child to find and draw two same-length things. Keywords name the comparison criterion (same, length).

parts.answer_key: Any 2 objects in the classroom that are the same length. Common: two pencils, two markers, two same blocks, two same shoes.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, find 1 thing that is LONGER than your hand. Draw it.
teacher_notes: Lesson 1 consolidation artifact. Hand out at the end of the Action phase. Most children should complete Part 1 with one prompt. Part 2 may need scaffolding for the 'mixed order' reasoning. Use Part 1 as the primary diagnostic signal — children who circle the wrong object on visually-tilted pairs need the 'line up at one end' re-loop.
